blocks.text: 1.2.2 For Loops in Java
Concept Explanation

For loops in Java provide a compact way to iterate over a range of values or elements in a collection. They are particularly useful when you know in advance how many times you want to execute a block of code.
Key Points to Remember

items: Basic syntax: `for (initialization; condition; update) { // code block }`
The initialization, condition, and update parts are optional.
Multiple variables can be initialized and updated in a for loop.
The scope of variables declared in the initialization is limited to the loop.
Infinite loops can be created with `for (;;) { // code block }`

blocks.text: Java 21 Features

items: Enhanced for loop (for-each, available since Java 5): `for (Type item : collection) { // code block }`
Use with the `var` keyword for local variable type inference (Java 10+).

blocks.text: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

items: Off-by-one errors: Be careful with loop bounds, especially when using `<=` or `>=`.
Modifying loop variables inside the loop body can lead to unexpected behavior.
Forgetting to update the loop variable can result in infinite loops.
Using floating-point values for loop counters can cause precision issues.

blocks.text: Best Practices and Optimization Techniques

items: Use enhanced for loops when iterating over collections or arrays.
Avoid unnecessary object creation inside loops.
Consider using `StringBuilder` for string concatenation in loops.
Extract loop-invariant computations outside the loop.
Use appropriate data structures to minimize nested loops.

blocks.text: Edge Cases and Their Handling

items: Empty collections or arrays: Ensure your code handles these gracefully.
Large number of iterations: Be aware of potential integer overflow.
Breaking out of nested loops: Use labeled breaks when necessary.

blocks.text: Interview-specific Insights

items: Be prepared to write loops on a whiteboard or in a code editor without auto-completion.
Understand when to use for loops vs. while loops or Java 8+ Stream operations.
Be familiar with common loop patterns (e.g., finding max/min, accumulating results).

items: Initialization: Executed once at the beginning of the loop.
Condition: Checked before each iteration.
Update: Executed at the end of each iteration.

items: `break`: Terminates the loop entirely and transfers control to the statement immediately following the loop.
`continue`: Skips the rest of the current iteration and moves to the next iteration of the loop.
